title: Calling free in a procedure in C
body_html:
In this procedure, I am trying to copy 'b' characters of a string 'c' into an array of strings. So I created a local variable 'ans'. If I call free like I do, my program doesn't output anything (because I free'd it) and valgrind gives me a bunch of errors. If I don't call free, I only get 1 error of memory leak. How do I free 'ans'?

void foo(void**av, void*bv, void*cv) {
    char** a = (char**) av;
    intptr_t b = (intptr_t) bv;
    char* c = (char*) c;

    char* ans = malloc(b*sizeof(char));
    int i = 0;
    while(c[i]!=0 && i<b)
        ans[i] = c[i++];
    ans[i] = 0;
    *a = ans;
    free (ans);
}

events.body_html: you can free ans from the caller function of foo()...

I think you're misunderstanding what free (ans); does. It doesn't free ans itself -- it still has the same value it always had. It frees the block you allocated when you called malloc. Since the caller still needs to access that block (that's why you did *a = ans; -- to let the caller access the memory you allocated), you can't free it except in the caller, after they're done with it.
